dropped.finding: The new host_logs_not_arriving alarm wraps a SINGLE metric (m = IncomingLogEvents) in FILL(m, 0) with no sibling metric to supply a time grid. The repo's own monitoring_membound.tf documents that 'FILL over a metric with NO datapoints in the window' fails silently and relies on a second always-publishing metric for its grid; when shipping stops completely the IncomingLogEvents series has no datapoints, so FILL(m,0) may produce no zeros and the alarm would fall back to treat_missing_data=breaching -- reintroducing the evaluation-range aging that caused the measured 26m47s delay.
scenarios: CloudWatch agent stops entirely so IncomingLogEvents publishes zero datapoints for the whole window; FILL(m,0) has no time grid and emits nothing, the alarm relies on breaching-missing semantics and may again page only after the last real datapoint ages out of the evaluation range (the original ~27 min failure).

dropped.finding: The offline detection-bound test models worst-case detection solely from (period, evaluation_periods, filled) and hard-codes 'filled => bounded', so it will pass any alarm that merely contains the string expression="FILL(m, 0)" regardless of whether the FILLed metric has a time-grid source. It cannot detect the single-metric self-FILL gap it is meant to guard against.
scenarios: A future edit (or this very alarm) that FILLs a sometimes-absent single metric still passes test_shipping_stopped_alarm_pages_within_fifteen_minutes, giving false assurance that the 15-minute bound holds.
